# useScrollPosition

> Lightweight hooks for scroll position detection

## Get started

Need reliable scroll data for `animations`, `lazy loading`, or `sticky UI`?

`@n8tb1t/use-scroll-position` gives you a `lightweight`, `tree-shakable` set of `hooks` that detect scroll position for the `viewport` or any `element` inside it — making scroll-driven `UX` easy to build.

### [useWindowScrollPosition](/use-window-scroll-position)

Track the global window scroll position or a specific element position by attaching the returned ref.
Supports detecting when the viewport or element reaches the top or bottom.

### [useBodyScrollPosition](/use-body-scroll-position)

Like useWindowScrollPosition, but uses a different detection method under the hood.

### [useOverflowScrollPosition](/use-overflow-scroll-position)

Track scrolling inside an overflow container. Provides both rootRef (for the container) and targetRef (for a child element) to detect scroll position and top/bottom reach within that container.


import { Callout } from 'vocs/components'

import { TrackBodyScrollPosition } from '../components/track-body-scroll-position'
import { TrackElementPositionBody } from '../components/track-element-position-body'

## useBodyScrollPosition

<Callout type="success">
  Just like <b>useWindowScrollPosition</b>, <b>useBodyScrollPosition</b> lets you track scrolling — but under the hood it uses a different method to detect position.
</Callout>

Lets you track scrolling on the `global page`. It returns a `callback` that can be passed as a `ref` to any child element. When used this way, it tracks the scroll position of that element instead of the `window`.

You can use this hook to:

* Track global window scroll position.
* Track the scroll position of a specific element by passing the returned callback as a ref.
* Detect when the scroll reaches the top or bottom of the viewport.
* Detect when the specific element on the page reaches the top or bottom of the viewport.

### API

```ts
import { useBodyScrollPosition } from '@n8tb1t/use-scroll-position'

/**
 * Tracks the scroll position of the window or a specific element.
 * 
 * @param callback - Function called on scroll 
 * with previous and current positions.
 * @param options - Optional configuration object.
 */
useBodyScrollPosition(callback, option)
```

### Callback

```ts
/**
 * Callback object passed to the `useBodyScrollPosition` callback function.
 */
interface UseBodyScrollPositionCallbackOptions {
  /** Previous scroll position */
  prevPos: { x: number; y: number }
  
  /** Current scroll position */
  currPos: { x: number; y: number }

  /** True if scrolled to the top */
  top: boolean

  /** True if scrolled to the bottom */
  bottom: boolean
}
```

### options

```ts
/**
 * Optional configuration object for the hook.
 */
interface Options {
  /** Number of milliseconds to wait before calling the callback (throttle) */
  await: number
}
```

### Basic example

:::code-group
<div data-title="Preview">
  <TrackBodyScrollPosition />
</div>

```tsx [track-body-scroll-position.tsx]
import { useBodyScrollPosition } from '@n8tb1t/use-scroll-position'
import { useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react'

import { LoremIpsum, NavLinks, Panel } from '$components'

export const Navbar = () => {
  const rendersCount = useRef(0)

  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(true)

  useBodyScrollPosition(({ prevPos, currPos, top, bottom }) => {
    setVisible(top || (!bottom && currPos.y >= prevPos.y))
  }, {})

  return useMemo(
    () => (
      <div>
        <Panel visible={visible} placement="top">
          <NavLinks variant="orange" />
        </Panel>
        <LoremIpsum />
        <Panel className="items-center" placement="bottom">
          <div className="flex gap-1 bg-orange-400 p-2 text-sm text-white">
            Renders count:
            <span className="text-gray-800">{++rendersCount.current}</span>
          </div>
        </Panel>
      </div>
    ),
    [visible]
  )
}
```
:::

### Track element position

Here, we attach the callback from `useBodyScrollPosition` to the `HTML` element via a ref. Now you can easily track the element’s position and know when it hits the top or bottom of the viewport.

:::code-group
<div data-title="Preview">
  <TrackElementPositionBody />
</div>

```tsx [track-element-position.tsx]
import {
  useBodyScrollPosition,
  type UseBodyScrollPositionCallbackOptions
} from '@n8tb1t/use-scroll-position'
import { useMemo, useState } from 'react'

import { cn, LoremIpsum, NavLinks, Panel } from '$components'

export const UseBodyPosition = () => {
  const [redBoxPosition, setRedBoxPosition] =
    useState<UseBodyScrollPositionCallbackOptions>()

  const setRedBoxRef = useBodyScrollPosition(setRedBoxPosition)

  return useMemo(
    () => (
      <div>
        <Panel placement="top">
          <NavLinks variant="orange" />
        </Panel>
        <LoremIpsum length={1} />
        <div
          ref={setRedBoxRef}
          className={cn(
            'top-[250px] isolate ml-12 flex w-fit gap-2 rounded-sm bg-orange-400 p-4 text-orange-950 ring-3 ring-orange-600 ring-inset',
            {
              'bg-green-400 text-green-950 ring-green-600': redBoxPosition?.top,
              'bg-red-400 text-red-950 ring-red-600': redBoxPosition?.bottom
            }
          )}
        >
          <span>X:{redBoxPosition?.currPos?.x}</span>
          <span>Y:{redBoxPosition?.currPos?.y}</span>
        </div>
        <LoremIpsum />
      </div>
    ),
    [redBoxPosition, setRedBoxRef]
  )
}
```
:::


import { TrackOverflowScrollPosition } from '../components/track-overflow-scroll-position'
import { TrackElementPositionOverflow } from '../components/track-element-position-overflow'

## useOverflowScrollPosition

`useOverflowScrollPosition` is a React hook for tracking the scroll position inside a scrollable container with `overflow`.
It returns two ref setters:

* `rootRef` – attach this to the scrollable container (the element with overflow).
* `targetRef` (optional) – attach this to a child element inside the container if you want to track its position relative to the container.

You can use this hook to:

* Track container’s current scroll position (`x`, `y`).
* Track the scroll position of a specific element by passing the returned callback as a ref.
* Detect when the scroll reaches the top or bottom of the viewport.
* Detect when the specific element on the page reaches the top or bottom of the viewport.

### API

```ts
import { useOverflowScrollPosition } from '@n8tb1t/use-scroll-position'

/**
 * Tracks the scroll position of the window or a specific element.
 * 
 * @param callback - Function called on scroll 
 * with previous and current positions.
 * @param options - Optional configuration object.
 */
useOverflowScrollPosition(callback, option)
```

### Callback

```ts
/**
 * Callback object passed to the `useOverflowScrollPosition` callback function.
 */
interface UseOverflowScrollPositionCallbackOptions {
  /** Previous scroll position */
  prevPos: { x: number; y: number }
  
  /** Current scroll position */
  currPos: { x: number; y: number }

  /** True if scrolled to the top */
  top: boolean

  /** True if scrolled to the bottom */
  bottom: boolean
}
```

### options

```ts
/**
 * Optional configuration object for the hook.
 */
interface Options {
  /** Number of milliseconds to wait before calling the callback (throttle) */
  await: number
}
```

### Basic example

:::code-group
<div data-title="Preview">
  <TrackOverflowScrollPosition />
</div>

```tsx [track-overflow-scroll-position.tsx]
import { useOverflowScrollPosition } from '@n8tb1t/use-scroll-position'
import { useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react'

import { LoremIpsum, NavLinks, Panel } from '$components'

export const Overflow = () => {
  const rendersCount = useRef(0)

  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(true)

  const [setRootRef] = useOverflowScrollPosition(
    ({ prevPos, currPos, top, bottom }) => {
      setVisible(top || (!bottom && currPos.y <= prevPos.y))
    }
  )

  return useMemo(
    () => (
      <div ref={setRootRef} className="h-screen overflow-auto">
        <Panel visible={visible} placement="top">
          <NavLinks variant="orange" />
        </Panel>
        <LoremIpsum />
        <Panel className="items-center" placement="bottom">
          <div className="flex gap-1 bg-orange-400 p-2 text-sm text-white">
            Renders count:
            <span className="text-gray-800">{++rendersCount.current}</span>
          </div>
        </Panel>
      </div>
    ),
    [visible, setRootRef]
  )
}
```
:::

### Track element position

Here, we attach the callback from `useOverflowScrollPosition` to the HTML element via a ref. Now you can easily track the element’s position and know when it hits the top or bottom of the viewport.

:::code-group
<div data-title="Preview">
  <TrackElementPositionOverflow />
</div>

```tsx [track-element-scroll-position.tsx]
import {
  useOverflowScrollPosition,
  type UseOverflowScrollPositionCallbackOptions
} from '@n8tb1t/use-scroll-position'
import { useMemo, useState } from 'react'

import { cn, LoremIpsum } from '$components'

export const UseOverflowPosition = () => {
  const [redBoxPosition, setRedBoxPosition] =
    useState<UseOverflowScrollPositionCallbackOptions>()

  const [setRootRef, setRedBoxRef] =
    useOverflowScrollPosition(setRedBoxPosition)

  return useMemo(
    () => (
      <div ref={setRootRef} className="h-dvh overflow-auto">
        <LoremIpsum length={2} />
        <div
          ref={setRedBoxRef}
          className={cn(
            'top-[250px] isolate ml-12 flex w-fit gap-2 rounded-sm bg-orange-400 p-4 text-orange-950 ring-3 ring-orange-600 ring-inset',
            {
              'bg-green-400 text-green-950 ring-green-600': redBoxPosition?.top,
              'bg-red-400 text-red-950 ring-red-600': redBoxPosition?.bottom
            }
          )}
        >
          <span>X:{redBoxPosition?.currPos?.x}</span>
          <span>Y:{redBoxPosition?.currPos?.y}</span>
        </div>
        <LoremIpsum length={4} />
      </div>
    ),
    [redBoxPosition, setRedBoxRef, setRootRef]
  )
}
```
:::


import { TrackWindowScrollPosition } from '../components/track-window-scroll-position'
import { TrackElementPositionWindow } from '../components/track-element-position-window'

## useWindowScrollPosition

Lets you track scrolling on the `global page`. It returns a `callback` that can be passed as a `ref` to any child element. When used this way, it tracks the scroll position of that element instead of the `window`.

You can use this hook to:

* Track global window scroll position.
* Track the scroll position of a specific element by passing the returned callback as a ref.
* Detect when the scroll reaches the top or bottom of the viewport.
* Detect when the specific element on the page reaches the top or bottom of the viewport.

### API

```ts
import { useWindowScrollPosition } from '@n8tb1t/use-scroll-position'

/**
 * Tracks the scroll position of the window or a specific element.
 * 
 * @param callback - Function called on scroll 
 * with previous and current positions.
 * @param options - Optional configuration object.
 */
useWindowScrollPosition(callback, option)
```

### Callback

```ts
/**
 * Callback object passed to the `useWindowScrollPosition` callback function.
 */
interface UseWindowScrollPositionCallbackOptions {
  /** Previous scroll position */
  prevPos: { x: number; y: number }
  
  /** Current scroll position */
  currPos: { x: number; y: number }

  /** True if scrolled to the top */
  top: boolean

  /** True if scrolled to the bottom */
  bottom: boolean
}
```

### options

```ts
/**
 * Optional configuration object for the hook.
 */
interface Options {
  /** Number of milliseconds to wait before calling the callback (throttle) */
  await: number
}
```

### Basic example

:::code-group
<div data-title="Preview">
  <TrackWindowScrollPosition />
</div>

```tsx [track-window-scroll-position.tsx]
import { useWindowScrollPosition } from '@n8tb1t/use-scroll-position'
import { useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react'

import { LoremIpsum, NavLinks, Panel } from '$components'

export const Sidebar = () => {
  const rendersCount = useRef(0)

  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(true)

  useWindowScrollPosition(({ prevPos, currPos, top, bottom }) => {
    setVisible(top || (!bottom && currPos.y <= prevPos.y))
  })

  return useMemo(
    () => (
      <div>
        <Panel visible={visible} placement="left">
          <NavLinks variant="blue" />
        </Panel>
        <LoremIpsum />
        <Panel className="items-center" placement="bottom">
          <div className="flex gap-1 bg-orange-400 p-2 text-sm text-white">
            Renders count:
            <span className="text-gray-800">{++rendersCount.current}</span>
          </div>
        </Panel>
      </div>
    ),
    [visible]
  )
}
```
:::

### Track element position

Here, we attach the callback from `useWindowScrollPosition` to the HTML element via a ref. Now you can easily track the element’s position and know when it hits the top or bottom of the viewport.

:::code-group
<div data-title="Preview">
  <TrackElementPositionWindow />

```tsx [track-element-scroll-position.tsx]
import {
  useWindowScrollPosition,
  type UseWindowScrollPositionCallbackOptions
} from '@n8tb1t/use-scroll-position'
import { useMemo, useState } from 'react'

import { cn, LoremIpsum, NavLinks, Panel } from '$components'

export const Position = () => {
  const [redBoxPosition, setRedBoxPosition] =
    useState<UseWindowScrollPositionCallbackOptions>()

  const setRedBoxRef = useWindowScrollPosition(setRedBoxPosition)

  return useMemo(
    () => (
      <div>
        <Panel placement="top">
          <NavLinks variant="orange" />
        </Panel>
        <LoremIpsum length={1} />
        <div
          ref={setRedBoxRef}
          className={cn(
            'top-[250px] isolate ml-12 flex w-fit gap-2 rounded-sm bg-orange-400 p-4 text-orange-950 ring-3 ring-orange-600 ring-inset',
            {
              'bg-green-400 text-green-950 ring-green-600': redBoxPosition?.top,
              'bg-red-400 text-red-950 ring-red-600': redBoxPosition?.bottom
            }
          )}
        >
          <span>X:{redBoxPosition?.currPos?.x}</span>
          <span>Y:{redBoxPosition?.currPos?.y}</span>
        </div>
        <LoremIpsum />
      </div>
    ),
    [redBoxPosition, setRedBoxRef]
  )
}
```
